references.version_or_date: page lists plan years 2026 and 2027; read 2026-11-15

claims.text: Out-of-pocket maximum is the yearly ceiling on what you pay for covered in-network care (key takeaway, deductible section, FAQ 1)
claims.quote: The most you have to pay for covered services in a plan year. After you spend this amount on deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance for in-network care and services, your health plan pays 100% of the costs of covered benefits.

claims.text: 2026 Marketplace limit no more than $10,600 individual / $21,200 family; 2027 $12,000 / $24,000 (takeaway, limits section, FAQ 2, family section)
claims.quote: The out-of-pocket limit for a Marketplace plan for plan year: 2026: No more than $10,600 for an individual or $21,200 for a family 2027: No more than $12,000for an individual or $24,000 for a family

claims.text: Deductibles, copays and coinsurance for in-network covered care count; once reached the plan pays 100% of covered benefits (what-counts section, deductible section, FAQ 3, FAQ 4)
claims.quote: After you spend this amount on deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance for in-network care and services, your health plan pays 100% of the costs of covered benefits.

claims.text: Premiums, uncovered services, out-of-network care and costs above the allowed amount do not count (takeaway, exclusions list, FAQ 3, FAQ 9, planning section 'not counting premiums')
claims.quote: The out-of-pocket limit doesn't include: Your monthly premiums ... Anything you spend for services your plan doesn't cover ... Out-of-network care and services ... Costs above the allowed amount for a service that a provider may charge

claims.text: FAQ 6: premium does not count; you pay it whether or not you use care
claims.quote: The out-of-pocket limit doesn't include: Your monthly premiums ... A monthly amount you pay for coverage whether you get services or not.

claims.text: Deductible spending counts toward the out-of-pocket maximum, so the deductible is part of the ceiling
claims.quote: After you spend this amount on deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance for in-network care and services

references.notes: Figures are labeled by HealthCare.gov as Marketplace-plan limits; the page now says so. The glossary pop-up text for 'premiums' sits inline in the page.

claims.text: Deductible is what you pay for covered services before the plan starts to pay; many plans pay for certain services, like a checkup, before it is met (deductible section, FAQ 1)
claims.quote: The amount you pay for covered health care services before your insurance plan starts to pay. ... Many plans pay for certain services, like a checkup or disease management programs, before you've met your deductible.

claims.text: After the deductible you usually pay copays or coinsurance
claims.quote: After you pay your deductible, you usually pay only a copayment or coinsurance for covered services.

references.notes: Replaces old ref 2 (HealthCare.gov, Out-of-pocket costs), which did not say what counts toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

claims.text: Worked example: $3,000 deductible, 20% coinsurance, $12,000 allowed costs; you pay $3,000 + $1,800 = $4,800, below the example plan's $6,850 out-of-pocket maximum (plan pays $7,200 by arithmetic)
claims.quote: Allowable costs are $12,000. Deductible: $3,000 Coinsurance: 20% Out-of-pocket maximum: $6,850 ... So your total out-of-pocket costs would be $4,800

claims.text: Figure, $25,000 year: once costs reach $6,850 you pay only that and the plan pays for covered services for the rest of the plan year (split $3,000 + $3,850 and plan's $18,150 are arithmetic)
claims.quote: If your total out-of-pocket costs reach $6,850, you'd pay only that amount, including your deductible and coinsurance. The insurance company would pay for all covered services for the rest of your plan year.

claims.text: FAQ 4: after reaching the maximum the plan pays for covered services for the rest of the plan year
claims.quote: The insurance company would pay for all covered services for the rest of your plan year.

references.record_journal: Urban Institute (research brief, Bowen Garrett and John Holahan)

claims.text: In 2026 Part B has a $283 yearly deductible and 20 percent coinsurance on most services, and there is no cap on cost-sharing payments in traditional Medicare
claims.quote: In 2026, Part B has a deductible of $283 per year and requires 20 percent coinsurance on most services. There is no cap on cost-sharing payments in traditional Medicare (TM).

references.notes: Policy research brief, not a government source; now used only for the Part B figures and the no-cap statement. The 'which is why Medigap exists' wording was removed; Medicare.gov (ref 8) is cited for the Medigap point.

references.record_title: FAQs About Affordable Care Act Implementation (Part XXVII)
references.record_journal: U.S. Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and the Treasury

claims.text: Since 2016 the self-only (individual) limit applies to each person, including someone in family coverage (takeaway, family section, FAQ 7)
claims.quote: the self-only maximum annual limitation on cost sharing applies to an individual who is enrolled in family coverage or other coverage that is not self-only coverage under a group health plan.

claims.text: Applies from 2016 plan years
claims.quote: The Departments will apply this clarification only for plan or policy years that begin in or after 2016.

claims.text: Aggregate family limit: one person stops at the individual limit while family total continues to the plan's aggregate limit
claims.quote: cost sharing for individual #1 for 2016 is limited to $6,850, and the plan is required to bear the difference

claims.text: A plan may set a limit below the federal maximum
claims.quote: a plan is permitted to set an annual limitation below the maximum established under section 1302(c)(1)

claims.text: Grandfathered plans are not subject to the rule (it applies to non-grandfathered plans)
claims.quote: PHS Act section 2707(b) applies this requirement to all non-grandfathered group health plans, including non-grandfathered self-insured and large group health plans.

claims.text: 2025 limits were $9,200 and $18,400
claims.quote: the 2025 maximum annual limitation on cost sharing is $9,200 for self-only coverage and $18,400 for other than self-only coverage.

claims.text: There is a federal ceiling on how high a plan can set the limit
claims.quote: cost sharing for self-only coverage may not exceed the dollar limit for calendar year 2014 increased by an amount equal to the product of that amount and the premium adjustment percentage for 2027.

claims.text: Federal limits: 2027 $12,000 self-only / $24,000 other; 2026 $10,600 / $21,200 (takeaway, limits section, FAQ 2)
claims.quote: the 2027 maximum annual limitation on cost sharing is $12,000 for self-only coverage and $24,000 for other than self-only coverage. This represents an approximately 13.2 percent increase from the 2026 parameters of $10,600 for self-only coverage and $21,200

claims.text: 2027 reduced (CSR) limit $4,000 self-only / $8,000 other for household income 100 to 200 percent FPL
claims.quote: establishing the values of the 2027 reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing at $4,000 for enrollees with household income greater than or equal to 100 percent of the federal poverty level (FPL)

claims.text: Other-than-self-only reduced limit $8,000 and the 150-200 percent FPL band
claims.quote: Individuals eligible for CSRs under § 155.305(g)(2)(ii) (household income greater than 150 and less than or equal to 200 percent of FPL) | $4,000 | $8,000

references.notes: New primary source for the 2026 and 2027 federal limits and the 2027 CSR limits. CMS uses 'self-only' and 'other than self-only'; the guide's 'individual' and 'family' follow HealthCare.gov.

claims.text: Original Medicare has no yearly out-of-pocket limit unless you have supplemental coverage such as Medigap or join a Medicare Advantage Plan (takeaway, Medicare section, FAQ 8)
claims.quote: There's no yearly limit on what you pay out-of-pocket, unless you have supplemental coverage, like a Medicare Supplement Insurance (Medigap) policy or join a Medicare Advantage Plan (Part C)

claims.text: Medigap usually helps pay your share of costs like deductibles and coinsurance for Part A and Part B services
claims.quote: Medigap usually helps pay your portion of the costs (like deductibles and coinsurance) for services that Part A and Part B cover in Original Medicare.

references.notes: New source; replaces the Urban brief for the Medigap and no-yearly-limit statements.

claims.text: A plan year is a 12-month period that may not match the calendar year; check plan documents or ask your employer (planning section, FAQ 5)
claims.quote: A 12-month period of benefits coverage under a group health plan. This 12-month period may not be the same as the calendar year. To find out when your plan year begins, you can check your plan documents or ask your employer.

references.notes: New source; replaces the unsourced 'usually on January 1' and 'reset in January' wording.

claims.text: If your income qualifies you for cost-sharing reductions, you must pick a Silver plan to get the extra savings on out-of-pocket costs
claims.quote: If you qualify for cost-sharing reductions: You must pick a plan in the Silver category ... to get these extra savings on out-of-pocket costs.
